newsitem.title: CANADA: Striking Cargill Alberta workers reject offer.
newsitem.headline: Striking Cargill Alberta workers reject offer.

text.p: Cargill Foods Ltd said on Monday that striking meat packers at its Alberta processing plant rejected the company's latest contract offer.

Cargill Vice President Barb Isman said in a telephone interview that the proposal was the company's final offer to the 1,600 unionized workers who went on strike last Thursday at the 4,000 head of cattle-a-day slaughter plant in High River, Alberta.
She said that 91 percent of the unionized workers rejected the deal.
"We will complete processing of the inventory in the plant and then make a determination of where to go from there," Isman said.
"The use of replacement workers is our last choice but it may be our only choice," she added.
The United Food and Commercial Workers sought a C$1.95 an hour raise over three years while Cargill's last offer was C$1.50 over three years, Isman said.
